items.evidence: The acceptance test passes and asserts the exact marker 'sudo -n dpkg --configure -a\nran\n', the stdout line and exit 0. My holdout check ran the real CLI with a journal entry that is a subdirectory and a command that exits 7. sudo ran before the command, sudo's own stdout was passed through, 'finished' was logged and the wrapper exited 7. A second holdout check held the lock briefly and then released it: the wrapper waited, then recovered, then ran the command.

The test covers both an empty and a missing journal dir and asserts the marker is exactly 'ran\n'. My holdout check repeated both cases and saw no sudo call and exit 0. '--dpkg-updates' given without a value is rejected with a non-zero exit.

The test asserts the full ::warning:: line, that the command ran and exit 0. In my holdout check, a fake sudo exiting 5 produced 'failed (exit code 5); running sh -c ... anyway' and the command ran. With no sudo on PATH the command still ran with exit 0 and a ::warning:: line, but an extra ::error:: line also appeared (see J-1-02).
The test holds the lock with a live pid in a fake /proc/locks and asserts exit 1, the ::error::apt lock line, no 'interrupted' output and no marker file. The run passed locally and on CI.

The test passes in 15.1 s. It asserts elapsed under 30 s, timedOut true, exitCode -1, that the pid file exists and that the grandchild is gone within 2 s. My holdout check called runInSandbox directly with timeoutMs 8000. The probe spawned a sh that traps TERM and starts a background sleep (two descendant levels). The call returned in about 8 s with timedOut true and exitCode -1, and both descendant pids were dead afterwards. No stray processes or tlh-sandbox temp dirs were left.

The test asserts exitCode 0, timedOut false and output containing 'ok'. In my holdout check, a failing probe gave a real non-zero exit code (not -1), timedOut false, and output naming the failing test. A typecheck sandbox run gave exit 0. The full suite, including all locked callers, is green.

The static test checks the pin, path, key shape, month step, restore-keys, order, absence of if:, and the exact install run lines, step timeouts and job timeout. My holdout check parsed the YAML and compared it with the base commit: the 3 new steps plus 'Read month stamp' have no if: and no continue-on-error, they are placed in the right order, and all pre-existing steps are byte-for-byte unchanged.

findings.expected_vs_actual: Spec section 8 says apt hash-checks cached .debs against the signed index and downloads a tampered one again. The security review found that apt accepts a .deb already present in /var/cache/apt/archives on filename and size alone. The real trust boundary is who can write the Actions cache. This is a spec/documentation inaccuracy plus optional hardening, not a behaviour failure of any SPEC item.
findings.fix: Follow-up: correct section 8 (or the README/design notes). Optionally save the cache right after 'Collect apt archives' (cache/restore + cache/save split), and/or drop restored .debs whose sha256 does not match apt-cache show.

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected (A-2): when sudo cannot start, a single ::warning:: naming the reason. Actual: an ::error:: annotation ('could not start sudo ...') is printed first, then a ::warning:: saying '(exit code 1)'. The command still runs and the exit code is correct. This cannot happen on hosted runners.
findings.fix: Log only the ::warning:: with the real start-failure reason.

findings.expected_vs_actual: A-6 says the month key refreshes a stale set monthly. But restore-keys restores the previous month's entry, and Collect copies everything back, so superseded .debs accumulate across months until an entry is evicted.
findings.fix: Follow-up: drop restore-keys, or prune the collected set to the .debs from the current install (e.g. apt-get autoclean before Collect).

summary: All 9 SPEC items pass. AC#1 dpkg recovery, AC#2 process-group timeout and AC#3 cache wiring were verified by the suite plus independent holdout checks through the public CLI/API, including boundary and error inputs. The cold-then-warm CI runs confirm AC#3 on the warm path. The cold run hit a fast mirror, so the accepted slow-mirror limitation (Q-1) was not exercised. Test integrity is clean. There are no blocking findings; three LOW follow-ups remain (spec section 8 hash claim, the ::error:: on sudo start failure, stale .deb accumulation via restore-keys).
